title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Price increase
drivers.evidence: Recent week at $5.20 showed no uplift (x1.00 vs baseline); noise-adjusted promotion lift is x1.0; price increase is small and not proven to affect demand.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 27.4. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increased to $5.20 (+3.4% vs $5.03). Past promotions had a median uplift of x1.18, but the noise-adjusted estimate is only x1.0, indicating weak evidence. The most recent price change (2026-09-28) at $5.20 saw no lift (x1.00 vs baseline), suggesting this price change alone has no effect. No post-promotion dip is expected. The classical model suggests no effect, and the evidence for a price sensitivity effect is weak and inconsistent. The baseline already reflects recent seasonal trends. No driver justifies a change.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 27.4 | 5%-95%: 7.8 - 39.6 | 10%-90%: 10.3 - 39.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
